content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new here and also just starting with [product_name]. I'm developing a heater/cooler system using [product_name] and [product_name] operator device. The system should allow users to set a temperature between -20°C and +30°C. For instance, if the setpoint is -10°C, the cooler runs until that value is reached. If the setpoint is 20°C, the heater starts. I've managed to get the heater working, but I'm unable to set the setpoint below 0°C, meaning negative temperatures can't be input. Does anyone have any advice or solutions for this issue? Any support is appreciated. Block 008 is used as the up/down counter for the desired temperature, and block 016 is the comparator between the pt100 sensor and Block 008's value. Regards, [user_name]
This solution works perfectly. Thank you for the prompt response!

analysis.insight_summary: The main challenge discussed was the inability to input negative temperature values using the [product_name] device in a heating/cooling application, which restricted the system's capabilities for settings below zero degrees. A solution was quickly provided and successfully applied, with the user confirming its effectiveness.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the ability to set and use negative temperature values for full control over heating and cooling systems, specifically within a -20°C to +30°C range for more flexible operation.
